name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: domain 'chapter_23' (chapter ID 23 is a meaningful game ID in the valid 1-30 range, not address residue -- the function address 0x20aaf shares no digits with '23'), descriptor 'post_action'. Name accurately reflects the role: the chapter-23 turn-cycle post-action handler dispatched via the per-chapter handler table.
purpose: Chapter 23 turn-cycle post-action handler: evaluates the chapter's custom win/lose conditions and writes the chapter event/battle-end status code.
logic_summary: Does NOT call the default fd2_check_battle_end_condition; implements the full decision itself with two sequential independent writes to data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0x53ECC). Step 1 (LOSE): if any of the four protected chars runtime_char[0],[1],[0x10],[0x11] is dead (short-circuiting OR), set the code to 1. Step 2 (WIN): if the boss runtime_char[0x12] is dead, set the code to 2 unconditionally, so a boss kill overrides a LOSE (fall-through win-overrides-loss). Deadness is queried via fd2_check_char_is_dead per slot; no inline flag reads. Validated against the strategy guide: win condition = destroy mecha captain (slot 0x12); lose conditions = Sol/Sylphia/Caris/Rodman die (the four slots 0/1/0x10/0x11).

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Dispatch argument from the handler-table call site (conceptually an active char_idx/event arg). Unused by the body -- only consumed by the Watcom __CHK stack-probe prologue artifact; body has (void)event_arg.
params.reason: Descriptive, no address residue, and correctly conveys it is an ignored dispatch/event argument (the comment already documents it as the __CHK-prologue artifact).

returns.semantics: No return value; side effect is writing data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0 unchanged / 1 LOSE / 2 WIN).

reads_globals: data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr (indirectly, via fd2_check_char_is_dead which reads runtime_char[idx].flags bit0 for slots 0,1,0x10,0x11,0x12)
